_meta.description: Evidence-based 4-phase recovery framework for sports injuries. Data sourced from PubMed-indexed peer-reviewed literature. PMID sources cited for each phase.
_meta.framework_rationale: A biopsychosocial, criteria-based phased approach to rehabilitation is superior to time-based-only models (PMID 42205141, 41021821). The four phases align with tissue healing biology and functional capacity restoration.

phases.phase_duration_guidance: Days 1–7 (mild injuries) to weeks 1–6 (severe injuries / surgical)
phases.biological_basis: Inflammatory and proliferative phase of tissue healing. Vascular response, immune cell infiltration, and early fibroblast activity. Disrupting this phase delays repair.
goals: Protect injured tissue from further damage
Manage swelling, pain, and inflammation
Maintain non-injured areas active
Prevent disuse atrophy where possible
Begin gentle pain-free range of motion (ROM)
Establish therapeutic alliance and set recovery expectations
allowed_activities: POLICE protocol: Protection, Optimal Loading, Ice, Compression, Elevation
Pool walking or swimming (non-weight-bearing injuries)
Upper-body conditioning if lower limb injured
Isometric exercises in pain-free range
Gentle ROM exercises within pain threshold
Breathing exercises and nervous system down-regulation
Sleep optimization (≥8 hours; critical for tissue repair)
prohibited_activities: Weight-bearing if contraindicated by clinical findings
High-load resistance training of injured structure
NSAID overuse beyond 72h (impairs satellite cell-mediated repair in muscle injuries)

functional_milestones: Swelling stable or reducing
Pain not worsening with gentle ROM
Full weight-bearing tolerated (if lower limb) with normal gait
Isometric exercises tolerated without pain flare
criteria_to_advance.additional_criteria: Physician or physiotherapist sign-off for surgical cases; imaging clearance if fracture

coach_messaging_templates: Right now your body's repair crew is on the job – let them work. The goal this week isn't rest, it's smart loading.
Protection doesn't mean doing nothing. We're keeping everything else sharp while your {injury} heals.
Every day you follow the protocol is a day you get back sooner. Trust the process.
Ice, elevate, move gently. Your recovery has officially started.
phases.evidence_rationale: Italian Consensus Statement (PMID 31673400) and Bisciotti et al. support phased RTP with protection as phase 1. APKASS 2024 (PMID 42205141) emphasizes criteria-based advancement rather than fixed timelines. Optimal Loading (vs complete rest) is superior per current evidence (PMID 38642570).

phases.biological_basis: Proliferative phase: collagen synthesis, scar maturation, and early tensile strength restoration. Controlled loading stimulates appropriate collagen alignment.
goals: Restore full pain-free range of motion
Rebuild neuromuscular activation of injured structure
Address compensatory movement patterns
Progressive resistance training within pain tolerance
Restore proprioception and balance
Initiate eccentric strengthening when tolerated
allowed_activities: Progressive resistance training (pain-free range, low-to-moderate load)
Eccentric strengthening of injured muscle (when tolerated, NRS ≤3/10)
Proprioception and balance board exercises
Light cardiovascular conditioning (cycling, pool running, walking)
Core stability and kinetic chain exercises
Neuromuscular retraining (single-leg balance, perturbation training)
Sports massage and manual therapy as adjunct
Nutritional support: protein ≥1.6g/kg/day (PMID 23315753)

functional_milestones: Full pain-free ROM equal to contralateral
Single-leg stance ≥20 seconds without excessive sway
Strength deficit <30% vs contralateral on key muscle groups
No pain flare >24h after exercise sessions
Normal gait mechanics on treadmill (lower limb)
criteria_to_advance.additional_criteria: LSI on relevant strength testing ≥70% before progressing

coach_messaging_templates: Phase 2 is where real progress happens. We're teaching your body to move again – properly.
Your strength is coming back. Every rep is rebuilding the architecture that got you here.
Focus: full movement, full muscle activation, no compensations. Quality over everything.
We're restoring the foundation. Don't rush – what you build here determines when you get back.
phases.evidence_rationale: Eccentric protocols (L-protocol) significantly reduce reinjury rates in hamstring injuries (MD −1.95, PMID 40954668). Neuromuscular training is key to restoring proprioception post-ankle sprain (PMID 41385332). Protein intake ≥1.6g/kg/day supports muscle protein synthesis during recovery (PMID 23315753).

phases.phase_duration_guidance: Weeks 2–4 (mild) to weeks 8–24 (ACL, Achilles, RC repair)
phases.biological_basis: Remodeling phase: immature scar tissue replaced by organized collagen. Load stimulus required for optimal maturation. Neuromuscular control restoration is critical.
goals: Achieve ≥90% limb symmetry index (LSI) on strength testing
Restore sport-specific neuromuscular patterns
Build plyometric capacity (hop, bound, jump-land)
Introduce change of direction and agility training
Address psychological readiness (fear of reinjury screening)
Graduated running progression
Fatigue-resistance: ensure capacity to perform under match-level loads
allowed_activities: Progressive plyometrics: bilateral → unilateral, low-impact → high-impact
Change-of-direction drills at sub-maximal intensity (50–80% max)
Maximal-effort isokinetic testing to guide progression
Running program: intervals progressing to continuous runs
Sport-specific skill drills without contact
High-intensity interval training (cardio)
Mental imagery and confidence rebuilding exercises
ACL-RSI or Tampa Scale monitoring (PMID 33604148, 37681565)
prohibited_activities: Match play or live game simulations
Maximal speed without clearance from hop test battery
Returning to drills that consistently reproduce pain >NRS 2/10

functional_milestones: Quadriceps LSI ≥90% on isokinetic testing at 60°/s and 180°/s
Single-leg hop battery (SLH, triple hop, crossover hop, 6m timed) LSI ≥90%
Change of direction at ≥80% max velocity without pain or guarding
Bilateral drop-jump landing symmetry (no valgus collapse)
ACL-RSI score ≥65 (or equivalent psychological readiness scale)
No pain flare >24h post-maximal training session
Running at sport-specific velocity with normal mechanics
criteria_to_advance.additional_criteria: Physician and physiotherapist dual sign-off; ACL-RSI ≥65 for ACLR cases (OR 2.1–2.5 for successful RTS, PMID 40894294)

coach_messaging_templates: This is where athletes are made. You're not just rehabbing – you're rebuilding better.
Hop test at 90%? Check. Cutting at full pace? Almost there. You're closer than you think.
Trust the numbers. When your strength and movement are back, so are you.
The body's ready. Now we make sure the mind is too. Confidence is part of the criteria.
phases.evidence_rationale: LSI ≥90% on hop tests and isokinetic testing is the internationally accepted benchmark for RTS readiness (PMID 27423208, 40894294). Psychological readiness (ACL-RSI) is independently predictive of RTS success (PMID 35325002, 37681565). Bilateral drop-landing symmetry predicts reinjury risk after ACLR (PMID 41995908).

phases.phase_duration_guidance: 1–4 weeks transition period; graduated from training to full competition
phases.biological_basis: Ligament/tendon graft (if applicable) achieves 50–70% native strength by 6 months and up to 85–90% by 12–24 months. Sport demands must be titrated to tissue maturity.
goals: Full training participation without restriction
Match/competition-intensity exposure graduated
Confirm all RTS criteria met (physical + psychological)
Shared decision-making between athlete, clinician, coach
Ongoing monitoring for re-injury risk signals
Establish injury prevention program post-RTS
Load management plan for first 4–6 weeks post-RTS
allowed_activities: Full non-contact training at 100% intensity
Gradual contact exposure (modified contact → full contact)
Match simulation (training games)
Return to full competition
GPS/wearable load monitoring (PMID 31673400)
Ongoing neuromuscular prehab exercises
Psychological support continuation if needed
prohibited_activities: None (all activities permitted once criteria met)
NOTE: Activities should be graduated – avoid sudden jump to full competition volume

functional_milestones: All phase 3 criteria maintained
Full match-intensity training completed ≥3 sessions without adverse effects
Clinician, athlete, and coach all agree on readiness
Injury prevention program established
ACL-RSI ≥65–70 (ACLR); condition-specific psychological clearance
Load monitoring plan in place for first 4 weeks
criteria_to_advance.additional_criteria: Shared decision-making model (PMID 41021821, 42205141); biopsychosocial sign-off including physical, psychological, and contextual factors

coach_messaging_templates: You did everything right. This is what the work was for.
You're back. And not just back – better prepared than before.
Your first few games back, we're tracking your load carefully. Smart return keeps you in the game long-term.
The criteria are met. The team is ready for you. Let's go.
phases.evidence_rationale: Biopsychosocial, criteria-based, shared decision-making RTS is recommended by APKASS 2024 (PMID 42205141) and qualitative analysis of elite clinicians (PMID 41021821). GPS-based load monitoring at RTS reduces recurrence in football (PMID 31673400). ACL-RSI ≥70 at RTS significantly predicts successful return (PMID 40894294).
